mcqs.learning_point: Understand collective responsibility at a basic level
mcqs.question: The cabinet decides to increase indirect taxes. One minister publicly opposes the decision. According to the principle of collective responsibility, what must the minister do?

options.A: Continue to oppose the decision in Parliament and keep his ministerial post
options.B: Resign from the cabinet or publicly support the decision despite personal disagreement
options.C: Ask the President to overturn the decision
options.D: Ignore the principle as it applies only to the Prime Minister

mcqs.answer: Resign from the cabinet or publicly support the decision despite personal disagreement
mcqs.explanation: Collective responsibility means all ministers must stand by cabinet decisions. A minister who cannot do so must either resign or publicly endorse the decision. Options A, C and D ignore this constitutional doctrine.

mcqs.question: After a general election no single party secures a clear majority. What is the President’s constitutional role in forming the next government?

options.A: Appoint the leader of the party with the most seats as Prime Minister, irrespective of majority support
options.B: Dissolve the Lok Sabha and order fresh elections immediately
options.C: Invite the leader of the party or coalition that appears able to command a majority to form the government and prove it on the floor of the House
options.D: Appoint the Chief Justice of India as an interim Prime Minister

mcqs.answer: Invite the leader of the party or coalition that appears able to command a majority to form the government and prove it on the floor of the House
mcqs.explanation: When no party has a clear majority, the President invites the leader most likely to secure a majority to form the government and asks for a confidence vote. Options A and B ignore this process, and D is unrelated to the President’s duties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Prime Minister of India is a common misconception?

options.A: The Prime Minister is the head of the executive and leads the Council of Ministers
options.B: The Prime Minister is the ceremonial head of state representing India internationally
options.C: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President after elections
options.D: The Prime Minister must be a member of either House of Parliament

mcqs.answer: The Prime Minister is the ceremonial head of state representing India internationally
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of government, not the head of state; the President is the ceremonial head of state. Options A, C and D correctly describe the Prime Minister’s role.

mcqs.question: If the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, what must happen to the Council of Ministers?

options.A: Only the Prime Minister resigns, while other ministers continue in office
options.B: The entire Council of Ministers must resign
options.C: The President can replace the Prime Minister without affecting other ministers
options.D: The Council of Ministers remains in place until the next general election

mcqs.answer: The entire Council of Ministers must resign
mcqs.explanation: Under the doctrine of collective responsibility, loss of confidence in the Prime Minister means the whole Council must step down. Options A, C and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes the political executive from the permanent executive in India?

options.A: Political executive members are elected by the people, while permanent executive members are appointed by the President for life
options.B: Political executive changes with each government, whereas permanent executive consists of career civil servants who remain irrespective of political changes
options.C: Political executive handles foreign affairs only, while permanent executive handles domestic affairs only
options.D: Political executive has judicial powers, while permanent executive has legislative powers

mcqs.answer: Political executive changes with each government, whereas permanent executive consists of career civil servants who remain irrespective of political changes
mcqs.explanation: The political executive (President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers) is political and changes with elections. The permanent executive (bureaucracy) is career-based and continues across governments. Options A, C and D misrepresent their functions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand collective responsibility at a basic level
mcqs.question: In the Indian parliamentary system, the doctrine of collective responsibility means that:

options.A: Only the Prime Minister is accountable for the actions of the Council of Ministers
options.B: Each minister is individually responsible for his/her department, and the Council is not collectively accountable
options.C: The entire Council of Ministers shares responsibility for decisions, and must resign collectively if the Lok Sabha expresses no confidence
options.D: The President can dismiss any minister without consulting the Council

mcqs.answer: The entire Council of Ministers shares responsibility for decisions, and must resign collectively if the Lok Sabha expresses no confidence
mcqs.explanation: Collective responsibility binds all ministers to a common answerability; a no‑confidence vote forces the whole council to resign. Options A and B ignore the collective aspect, and D misstates presidential powers.

mcqs.question: What is the role of the President of India in the executive branch?

options.A: The President is the head of the judiciary
options.B: The President is the ceremonial head of the executive and appoints the Prime Minister
options.C: The President leads the legislative debates in Parliament
options.D: The President directly manages all ministries

mcqs.answer: The President is the ceremonial head of the executive and appoints the Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: The President is the constitutional (ceremonial) head of the executive and, on the basis of parliamentary composition, appoints the Prime Minister. Options A, C and D describe other branches or are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the position of the Prime Minister in India?

options.A: The Prime Minister is elected directly by the public in a separate election
options.B: The Prime Minister is the head of the judiciary
options.C: The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha and heads the Council of Ministers
options.D: The Prime Minister can serve without being a member of Parliament

mcqs.answer: The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha and heads the Council of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister must be a member of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) and is usually the leader of the party or coalition with majority support, heading the Council of Ministers. Options A, B and D are incorrect.
